gap: No result ChatGPT got states what the rated figures of the 16-inch 2560x1600 screens mean on one USB-C cable from a 16-inch MacBook Pro: the makers' watt figures are three different kinds of number (7.5 W typical, 11.0 W measured at full brightness, under 13 W ceiling), which is about 7.5% to 13% of the MacBook's 99.6 Wh battery per hour, and ASUS says its screen reaches maximum brightness only with the wall adapter plugged in.
standout_why: I read Macworld's best-for-Mac list and PCWorld's list in full. Macworld gives 350 nits, 2.9 lb and 65 W pass-through for the Duex Float 2 Pro and only 'Laptop battery drain' for the espresso Pro; it has no watt figure, no ppi and nothing on brightness when powered by the laptop. PCWorld gives one measured brightness (Arzopa Z1FC, 337 nits) and no draw figures, macOS scaling or bus-power limits. ChatGPT's own answer says only that a bus-powered monitor shortens battery life and that pass-through may not fully power a 16-inch Pro, with no numbers. Three cited pages could not be compared: the RTINGS article body did not load, TechRadar's page was cut off after its first pick, and seattlepi.com was blocked. RTINGS measures brightness and power in its reviews, so it may hold part of this.
decides: It confirms the Duex Float 2 Pro as the pick on the 16-inch 16:10 120 Hz line rather than changing it. Its 7.5 W is the lowest stated draw of the three, but that is a maker 'typical' figure set against a measured full-brightness figure and a maker ceiling, so the page should not call it the most efficient. Its 65 W pass-through is 46% of Apple's 140 W adapter, so it will not hold a 16-inch Pro's charge under heavy load. The ASUS MB16QHG's 500 nits should not be ranked on brightness as a one-cable figure. Two ChatGPT picks fall just short of the line: the Arzopa Z3FC ("2.5K" there means 2560x1440, 16:9, 16.1-inch) and the Arzopa Z1RC (60 Hz). No 2560x1600 screen matches the MacBook's sharpness: all sit near 189 ppi against Apple's 254 ppi.

findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's page for the 2024 M4 Pro / M4 Max model; I did not open a later model's page. Every normalised row below uses these figures.

findings.label: Pixel density of each panel class against the MacBook's 254 ppi
findings.source_title: MacBook Pro (16-inch, 2024) - Tech Specs - Apple Support
findings.note: Arithmetic: ppi = sqrt(width^2 + height^2) / diagonal in inches, on nominal diagonals; percentage is against Apple's 254 ppi. Only the 4K-class panels reach the MacBook's density; every 2560-wide 16-inch panel is about three quarters of it.

findings.label: Workspace at clean 2x scaling
findings.value: MacBook Pro 16 native 3456x2234 at 2x gives 1728x1117; a 2560x1600 panel at 2x gives 1280x800
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro Review - Mighty Gadget (James Smythe, 2026-08-16)
findings.note: Arithmetic on Apple's native resolution. James Smythe (Mighty Gadget) reports the same effect on Windows: 200% scaling at 2560x1600 leaves a working area 'closer to a 1280 x 800 canvas'. To get a MacBook-like workspace, a 2560x1600 panel must run at a non-integer scale. No macOS test was opened.

findings.label: Power draw as stated, against the MacBook's 99.6 Wh battery
findings.value: 7.5 W typical (maker's figure) = 7.5% of the battery per hour
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro feature - Gadget Pilipinas (Giancarlo Viterbo, 2026-10-22)
findings.note: Viterbo: 'Power draw is listed at 7.5W typical'. This is the maker's spec repeated, not a measurement, and the brightness setting behind 'typical' is not given. Arithmetic: 7.5 / 99.6. The draw is on top of the MacBook's own. Mobile Pixels' product page returned HTTP 429 on every attempt today.
